title: Email installation and recovery guarantees
summary: Understand immutable current-user releases, credential wrapper boundaries, matching documentation, and verified program rollback.
use_when: A caller or operator needs the supported Email program selection, publication, or rollback guarantees.
do_not_use_when: The goal is to prove live account readiness, authorize a message, or recover retained mail history.
outcome: A complete explanation of Email program installation, selectors, wrapper access, and supported retained-release recovery.
effects: Installation publishes immutable program and provider-bundle bytes and selects their current-user paths. Recovery verifies and selects a retained release.
Help/version checks and command registration read or send no mail. Private account settings remain separate from program release selection.
authority: Email owns its installed release integrity, wrappers, selectors and provider publication. The operator selects matching trusted tested artifacts and authorizes installation.
Resend and Gmail own account and mail readiness; requesters own message or occurrence authority.
success: Matching verified programs and their provider bundle are selected. A failed post-switch check restores selectors. Installer success establishes no real-send or receiving readiness.
failure_and_recovery: Reject foreign provider selectors and unverified retained releases. Resolve previous to its canonical owned directory and use a trusted tested installer for recovery.
Preserve the reported error after failed verification or selection; do not rewrite immutable releases or execute an unverified retained installer.
privacy: The wrapper extracts only the RESEND_API_KEY fallback from ~/.zshrc and starts the payload in a scrubbed environment. Credential bytes are absent from release artifacts and command arguments.
Explicit private account settings are separately retained. Installation/recovery probes bypass .zshrc and do not load mail credentials or mail content.
does_not_authorize: Remote account provisioning, credential changes, reading mail, sending a validation message, or taking over foreign selectors.

consumers.statement: Current-user macOS operators and installed callers can rely on the documented program selection and wrapper boundaries.

preconditions.statement: Install or recover only matching trusted tested artifacts from a validated candidate under the required operator authority. Manual selection needs absolute binary, bundle or owned release paths.

inputs.statement: Installation accepts a matching Email binary and provider bundle through the tested Rust installer. Recovery accepts an absolute canonical owned retained release. Usage registration selects the installed inventory.

outputs.statement: An immutable release and selected programs/documentation, or the installer error. Installation and recovery verify through help/version probes, never a real message.

data_semantics.statement: Release identity covers payload, wrapper, Rust installer, public layout and the full Chancery bundle. Provider publication describes that selected release; private account settings are outside the program-release selection.

identity_and_units.statement: Content hashes identify immutable releases beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Email/install/releases. current and previous name owned selections; no mail identity is created by installation.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Matching documentation follows the selected program release. Installation or registration establishes no current Resend/Gmail access, delivery or receiving observation.
No release-retention horizon or general installation-time service-availability objective is promised.

access.statement: The current-user paths are ~/.local/bin/email and ~/.local/bin/email-install. The wrapper preserves stdin and supplies only the credential fallback, HOME, fixed PATH and ordinary shell bookkeeping; explicit private credentials take precedence. Help/version probes bypass shell credential loading.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Identical bytes reuse a validated immutable release. Upgrade retains the superseded release through previous. Foreign provider selectors are refused and failed post-switch verification restores all selectors. Retained legacy and cell-install-v2 releases are verified before recovery; account settings remain separate.

operational_limits.statement: Email has no daemon, delivery database, scheduler or queue. Installation/recovery run only help/version checks. The provider selector is created even without Chancery, and the Email command remains usable without its binary or registry.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Immutable program release, provider publication and private account settings have separate identities and recovery boundaries. Legacy and cell-install-v2 retained releases are verified before selection.
No general cross-release support interval or retirement policy is promised.

reliances.statement: Ordinary committed-candidate delivery uses the Cell CI manager; explicit authorized manual installation uses matching tested artifacts. The manager owns its integration, validation, repair, deployment and outcome-email semantics.
